classification_basis: Independent mathematical mesh input facts; no solver outputs.

cases.name: planar-grid
cases.mathematical_reason: Two oriented unit-square triangles share only their diagonal; dual graph is one edge.

cases.name: planar-islands
cases.mathematical_reason: Cutting the shared diagonal yields two singleton face islands in one connected source mesh.

cases.name: cylinder-prism
cases.mathematical_reason: Four-sided open prism strip has a dual cycle cut by one vertical seam.

cases.name: frustum
cases.mathematical_reason: Four-sided frustum lateral strip is embedded; one vertical seam opens the dual cycle.

cases.name: cone
cases.mathematical_reason: Four cone side triangles meet in a manifold apex; one radial seam opens the dual cycle.

cases.name: branched-strip
cases.mathematical_reason: Central triangle with three outward neighbors has a star-shaped dual tree.

cases.name: tiny-triangle
cases.mathematical_reason: Nonzero orthogonal edges at tiny finite scale retain positive exact area.

cases.name: large-triangle
cases.mathematical_reason: Nonzero orthogonal edges at large finite scale retain positive exact area.

cases.name: near-degenerate
cases.mathematical_reason: Extremely thin finite triangle still has mathematically nonzero area; numerical acceptance remains verifier-owned.

cases.name: reversed-face
cases.mathematical_reason: Both faces traverse their shared edge in the same direction, violating consistent winding.

cases.name: duplicate-face
cases.mathematical_reason: Reversed vertex order still denotes the identical geometric triangle.

cases.name: nonmanifold-edge
cases.mathematical_reason: Three faces incident to edge (0,1) violate two-manifold incidence.

cases.name: bowtie-vertex
cases.mathematical_reason: The link of vertex zero has two disconnected components.

cases.name: degenerate
cases.mathematical_reason: All three points are collinear; exact cross product is zero.

cases.name: coplanar-intersection
cases.mathematical_reason: Consistent shared-edge winding but both faces occupy the same half-plane and overlap in positive area.

cases.name: disconnected
cases.mathematical_reason: Two separate triangular disks form a disconnected source mesh.

cases.name: uncut-cycle
cases.mathematical_reason: Uncut prism lateral strip has a cyclic dual graph.

cases.name: unsupported-curved-surface
cases.mathematical_reason: Version one accepts only explicit triangular meshes, never a NURBS description.

cases.name: exact-max-torus
cases.mathematical_reason: Periodic embedded 40 by 50 triangulated torus has 2000 vertices, 4000 faces and 6000 edges; all edges are cut.

result_vector.note: Serialization stress vector, not a numerically accepted layout. Fixed bounds: 1000 pairwise issues, 2 face IDs per issue, 64 Unicode code points per code, 256 per message, 16 warnings of 256 code points, 64 code points per solver/verifier version. Island IDs are deterministic ASCII island-{root_face_id}, at most 23 bytes. Free text uses four-byte UTF-8 code points.
